title: GDPR telemetry erasure gap: user_hash-keyed tables (raw_dumps, enriched_signals, consent_audit) cannot be deleted if hash is deterministic from Clerk ID

If HMAC with a per-user secret, key deletion = effective erasure (GDPR-safe). If bare sha256, a data authority can argue the rows are pseudonymous, not anonymous. This is a product/legal decision, not a pure code fix.

If bare sha256: migrate to HMAC(clerk_id, per-user-secret) where the secret is stored in a secrets table that IS included in the GDPR cascade. fix: No fix required. Already handled by upstreamError. Optionally normalize all upstream error responses to a fixed 502 regardless of upstream status code for strict information hiding.
ev: packages/worker-http/src/index.ts lines 44-63: upstreamError() logs `detail` server-side only and returns `json({ error: code, request_id: requestId }, status)` to the client — errText is NOT forwarded. Round 3 suspected this as a leak but the code confirms it is already handled. The residual risk: the upstream HTTP status code is passed as the second arg to upstreamError and echoed in the Response status (e.g., 502 for Supabase 409), which reveals that a 409 from Supabase occurred — but no column names or schema details leak.
ui: Minimal. An attacker learns the upstream returned a conflict (409→502) but no DB schema details are exposed.

title: partner_snapshots missing updated_at trigger — stale timestamps possible if caller omits field in future UPDATE
fix: Add a before-update trigger on partner_snapshots matching the pattern of other tables: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION partner_snapshots_touch() RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN NEW.updated_at := now(); RETURN NEW; END; $$; CREATE TRIGGER partner_snapshots_touch BEFORE UPDATE ON partner_snapshots FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE PROCEDURE partner_snapshots_touch();
ev: supabase/migrations/20260602103016_partner_bilateral_sync.sql line 44: updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now() — default only fires on INSERT, no before-update trigger. partner.ts line 189: putSnapshot manually sets updated_at in the upsert payload today. All other timestamp-bearing tables in the schema have a server-side trigger (encrypted_state_touch, profiles_touch, push_tokens_touch). Rounds 1 and 2 did not flag this.
ui: Invisible today. If any future code path issues an UPDATE without including updated_at, the timestamp stays stale — partner's client reads old mood/crisis state believing it is current.

title: workers/apns-push has a private json() helper instead of importing the identical export from @ollie/worker-http
fix: Add `'@ollie/worker-http': 'workspace:*'` to workers/apns-push/package.json. Replace local json() with `import { json } from '@ollie/worker-http'`.
ev: Round 3: workers/apns-push/src/index.ts:195 defines `function json(obj: unknown, status = 200): Response { return new Response(JSON.stringify(obj), { status, headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' } }); }`. @ollie/worker-http exports an identical helper. workers/apns-push/package.json does not list @ollie/worker-http as a dependency (while workers/ai-proxy, workers/cron, workers/sentry-tunnel all do).
ui: Minor. Any future change to the response format (e.g. adding a request-id header) must be applied in two places.
